content.title: Florida targets NFL’s ‘Rooney Rule’ promoting minority coaches
content.text: The move by Uthmeier aligns with ongoing attempts by Florida’s conservative leaders to rid the state of diversity, equity and inclusion-aligned policies, from public schools to colleges and now even local governments. But taking on the NFL, which prides itself on diversity programs like the Rooney Rule, would be a significant escalation of that fight.Created in 2003 by the NFL’s DEI Committee, the Rooney Rule as it exists today requires every team to interview at least two external minority candidates for open head coach, coordinator and general manager jobs. At the same time, the policy rewards teams for developing minority staff by granting them compensatory draft picks if a minority coach or executive is hired away by another franchise.But while the NFL touts these rules, Uthmeier contends that they “require precisely what Florida law forbids” by calling on teams to “limit, segregate, and classify applicants for certain employment and training opportunities because of race and sex.” Uthmeier copied several team and federal officials on his letter to the NFL, including Stephen Ross, chair and managing general partner of the Miami Dolphins; Bryan Glazer, owner and co-chair of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; and Shad Khan, owner of the Jacksonville Jaguars. The letter also went to Harmeet Dhillon, assistant attorney general for the Justice Departments’ Civil Rights Division, and Andrea Lucas, chair of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.NFL officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment surrounding Uthmeier’s letter.Named after late Pittsburgh Steelers owner Dan Rooney, the NFL’s diversity rule has its fair share of critics who contend it hasn’t done enough to actually propel Black coaches in the league. One top coordinator and former head coach, Brian Flores, is suing the NFL for alleged racial discrimination, claiming, among other things, that teams are conducting “sham” interviews to comply.Notably, the America First Legal Foundation, founded by White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, filed a civil rights complaint against the Rooney Rule in 2024, making similar claims as Florida’s current concerns. The status of that complaint is unclear.
